findings.issue: Snapshots retain only selected pair endpoints, dropping intermediary events and corpus context used by correlateEvents. A selected auto-cluster A-B connected through C replays without its cluster and is incorrectly scored as a false negative.

Row type is inferred from an optional event property instead of schema. Valid pair rows with extra event fields hide their real a/b references from family grouping and split-leakage validation, allowing the same event into tuning and holdout; CLI also routes resulting errors by the wrong discriminator.

An explicitly admitted ledger benchmark split is attached only to its matching pair. Other pairs in the same generated family retain the hash split, so a valid holdout ledger record can make the sampler's own output fail split-leakage validation.

Before/after comparison marks a location error resolved whenever its example disappears, including when a prediction becomes unknown and is excluded from scoring. This misreports lost coverage as a corrected role, precision or region.
Unlabeled pair candidates bypass benchmark enum validation, so benchmark=production is silently accepted even though this field already controls split isolation.
follow_up is counted as a same-event negative and contributes false positives when merged, but an unmerged follow_up never contributes a true negative, leaving the confusion counts incomplete.

needs-human: Both human annotation datasets are empty and the real candidates span only one week. Issue #43's human baseline and required hard-negative strata, including cross-month follow-ups, remain unfulfilled; synthetic tests cannot supply that acceptance evidence.

summary: Fixed six defects in replay corpus context, schema-based split isolation, ledger family splits, unknown-location comparisons, candidate split validation and follow-up confusion counts. Eleven regression cases went red-to-green; Git Bash verification passes 1036 Vitest tests, 5 Python tests, typecheck/build and operational checks. needs-human: human annotation datasets remain empty and real hard-negative coverage is incomplete, so issue #43 baseline acceptance remains pending; all fixes are local, with no push or deployment.
